title: The tablet
hook: the first thing anyone writes is a letter: Guru Nanak's Patti, a poem with one line of wisdom for each Gurmukhi letter

segments.voice: Yesterday we closed the Oankar, an alphabet that asks a teacher to listen. Your line was humble learning. Who did you teach, and what did they teach you back? Day one thousand one hundred fifty-four.

What was the first thing you ever wrote? Not a sentence. A letter. One shape, traced over and over, probably crooked, probably in a color you chose yourself. Before anyone writes a word, they learn to make the marks one at a time. Yesterday's poem took the alphabet and sang it to a scholar. Today's takes the alphabet back to the beginner's desk. In Raga Asa, on ang four thirty-two, Guru Nanak has a poem named for the thing a child wrote on. Today's word: Patti.
screen: `THE FIRST THING YOU EVER WROTE.` → `ONE SHAPE AT A TIME.` → `BACK TO THE BEGINNER'S DESK.`

segments.voice: Patti means a tablet, a writing board. Earlier on this path we heard the janamsakhi story of the boy Nanak at school, asking his teacher what the letters really point to. Today we open the poem itself. First, its shape. The Patti is an acrostic. Each stanza opens with a letter of the Gurmukhi alphabet, and that letter starts a line about God and the soul. Letter by letter, the alphabet becomes a path. Second, how it begins. It opens with sasai, the letter S, and a line about the One who made the world, which this path takes up tomorrow. Then comes eevrri, and in paraphrase: the Primal Being is the Giver, and that One alone is true. Then oorrai, and in paraphrase: praise the One whose limit no one has found. Three letters in, and the poem has said who made things, who gives, and that the giver can't be measured. Third, why a tablet. A writing board is where learning starts small. You don't begin with a library. You begin with one mark, then the next. The Patti uses that pace on purpose. It never asks for everything at once. It asks for one letter, and one line of wisdom to go with it. That's a way to learn anything deep: not all of it today, just the next letter. Fourth, notice the plain humility of the form. A writing board belongs to beginners, and the poem carries its name. The tablet stays a tablet. It just points further. Today's line: letter by letter.
screen: `PATTI: A WRITING BOARD.` · `AN ACROSTIC: ONE LETTER, ONE LINE.` · `IT OPENS WITH SASAI.` · `LEARNING AT THE PACE OF ONE MARK.` · then, large: `LETTER BY LETTER.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: write three letters. Take a pen and any scrap of paper. If you can, look up the three letters the Patti opens with: sasai, eevrri and oorrai. Copy those shapes slowly, one at a time, the way a beginner would. Don't rush them, and don't judge how they look. Say each name softly as you write it. If Gurmukhi isn't open to you right now, write the first three letters of any alphabet you know, just as slowly. Then put the pen down and sit with your breath. If you pray, you can say Waheguru once. The bell holds the time.
Patti. A writing board, and Guru Nanak's poem in Raga Asa that gives each Gurmukhi letter a line of wisdom. Today's word.
Your line: letter by letter. Today, when something big feels like too much to learn, do only the first small piece of it, and stop there on purpose. Day one thousand one hundred fifty-four.

screen: `DAY 1154 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: SASAI: HE MADE THE WORLD.`

howItsDone: In gurdwara Punjabi classes and at home, children learn the Gurmukhi letters, and teachers sometimes use the Patti to show that each letter can carry a line of the Guru's teaching.

original.note: patti: a writing board; the heading of Guru Nanak's alphabet poem in Raga Asa.

trapdoor: what you thought: patti is just a school slate.
what it means: it's also Guru Nanak's poem in Raga Asa that gives each letter a line of wisdom.
what a scholar hears: an acrostic that opens with sasai, eevrri, oorrai: who made things, who gives, and the One without limit.

sources.ref: Asa, Mahala 1, Patti, opening stanzas (sasai, eevrri, oorrai), Ang 432

notes: Patti opening paraphrased: sasai (the One who made the world is the one Master of all); eevrri ('eevrree aad purakh hai daataa aape sachaa soee'); oorrai ('oorrai upmaa taa kee keejai jaa kaa ant na paaiaa'). Please confirm order and paraphrase.

Practice: the modern Gurmukhi primer is given as opening oorra, airra, eerri, sassa, haha. This is general knowledge, not from the cited text; please confirm, and confirm the trapdoor's note that the Patti's order differs.
The earlier janamsakhi story is referred to (y1 day 24) without retelling it, to avoid repetition.
